title: Web Magnets — Caption Split
oneLiner: Tear a phrase and photo from two pages into a floating margin; slide words through the photo to open a tiny poster with source threads.
targetFeeling: I made those two things say something together: playful editorial surprise through spatial juxtaposition.
gesture: Drag a verbatim phrase across a photo's horizontal seam; attraction within 24 pixels previews the snap. Release to compose; pull the phrase away to unpair.
magicMoment: KEEP MOVING splits a snail photo into two intact halves around a white text band: an absurd motivational poster. TAKE YOUR TIME changes its meaning using the same rule.
example: Select KEEP MOVING on the authored Instructions for a busy day fixture; pin the words into the margin.
Pin the team's own snail photo from Things outside my window; one board holds three phrases and two photos.
Snap words into the snail's seam, then unpair and swap to TAKE YOUR TIME; both sources remain attached.
must: Two labelled localhost fixtures with three authored phrases and two team-owned photos: KEEP MOVING, TAKE YOUR TIME, DO NOT DISTURB, snail, spinning fan.
Explicit selection or image context-menu capture pins only the chosen item, with a lift animation; originals stay on the page.
One floating board shared across page invocations, local coordinates and provenance, maximum six inputs; five in the demo.
One physical snap grammar: separate intact image halves around a fitted verbatim text band, retain source tags, drag to unpair, one pair at a time.
Preserve exact text, owned asset ID, URL/title and anchor; a thin thread highlights a visible origin, while an off-page source uses a labelled return chip.
Live source return, phrase replacement after unpairing, and reset; both source tags remain visible on the composition.
nonGoals: Searchable archive, folders, accounts, or summariser.
AI rewriting or inferred relationships, multiple snap grammars, multi-image layouts, or typography editing.
Universal site support, arbitrary third-party artwork capture, or image/PDF export.

demo.action: Select KEEP MOVING on fixture A and pin it; show the lift into the margin.
Switch to B, invoke the margin, and pin the snail; three preloaded fixture selections complete the five-item board.
Snap the phrase into the photo seam; pause on the absurd split-photo poster.
Unpair and snap TAKE YOUR TIME into the same photo; explain that the person supplies the interpretation.
Hover both source tags, follow A's return chip, and show the exact original phrase highlighted.
Return to the poster: a thought made by putting two sources together.

buildPlan: Hour 1: prove seam transformation, reversal, and readable poster; cut decorative motion if needed.
Hour 2: connect live selection and owned-image capture on both fixtures; choose fallback if capture is unreliable.
Hour 3: shared local board state, provenance anchors, source return, and reset.
Hour 4: phrase swapping, pointer feedback, text fitting, and five-item layout.
Hour 5: acceptance checks, rehearsal, and scope freeze.
minimumStack: Plain JavaScript/CSS/SVG overlay, Manifest V3 extension, local state, two local HTML fixtures and team-owned photos; no framework, backend, or model.
realVsAuthored: Live: selection, drag, snap, unpair, source return. Authored: labelled fixture pages, phrases, owned photos, asset mappings, seam geometry and motion. Text and photos remain unchanged; juxtaposition and layout create the new composition. No semantic detection.
acceptanceChecks: Both source pages contribute to one five-item board without losing positions.
An unfamiliar tester snaps then unpairs a phrase/photo within ten seconds of seeing the seam cue.
Both source tags return to exact fixture origins; verbatim text survives phrase swapping.
risk: Reliable cross-page capture and source return within five hours; controlled anchors and owned assets bound the risk, while arbitrary web image retrieval is unproven.
fallback: The same two fixture documents inside one local demo shell with a persistent margin and live capture/snapping; disclose simulated navigation and absent extension integration.
verdict: Recommend the bounded fixture version. Improve magnetic clippings by making words physically open an image to become its voice; the transformation earns the concept beyond a moodboard.

sources.title: Chrome activeTab
sources.takeaway: Observed: user invocation grants temporary page access, revoked across origins. Inference: invoke on each source page and maintain board continuity separately in local state.

sources.title: Chrome contextMenus
sources.takeaway: Observed: selectionText, pageUrl and srcUrl are supplied. Inference: text capture is straightforward; an image URL does not establish retrievable bytes or reuse permission, so map owned fixture assets.

sources.title: Whitney Museum: John Baldessari
sources.takeaway: Observed: Whitney describes snapshots paired with didactic text and meaning changing with context. Inference: one verbatim imperative plus an incongruous owned photo can carry the demo; no artwork is copied.
